message.content: Eve needs real auth and canvas persistence. Please build Next.js route handlers for: signed cookie sessions, optimistic canvas autosave, and conflict handling when a client reconnects with stale local edits. Keep it provider-agnostic on storage and write tests for the conflict path.

content.text: Plan: three route handlers — POST /api/auth/login issues a signed (HMAC) cookie session, PUT /api/canvas/[id] does optimistic autosave keyed by a version counter, and on reconnect the client sends its lastVersion so we can detect and merge conflicts. I'll read the current auth stub and the canvas store first to match existing shapes.

Stub as expected. I'll sign sessions with an HMAC over {userId, issuedAt} using a server secret, set it as an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie, and verify it in middleware. Reading the canvas store so autosave writes the same element/version shape the client already uses.

Good — the store already has a monotonic version counter, which is exactly what the optimistic autosave and conflict detection need. Writing the auth route: HMAC-signed cookie, httpOnly + SameSite=Lax, with verifySession() shared by the canvas routes.

Now the verifySession helper and the autosave route. The rationale for optimistic autosave: the client PUTs its scene with the version it based the edit on, and if the stored version is higher we've decided to return 409 with the server scene rather than silently overwrite, so the client can reconcile.

Writing the autosave + conflict route. I settled on keeping storage behind a saveScene/loadScene adapter so it's provider-agnostic. The conflict rule, decided: if body.baseVersion < stored.version, return 409 with the server scene and version; otherwise persist and bump.

message.content: Good. On reconnect with stale local edits the client shouldn't just lose them — make the 409 path return enough for the client to merge, not overwrite.

content.text: Right — here's the rationale for the merge-not-overwrite path I've settled on. The 409 already returns the full server scene and its version; the client merges by replaying its un-acked local element ids onto the server scene (last-writer-wins per element id, server base) rather than discarding either side. I'll write the conflict tests around exactly that: stale baseVersion → 409 with server scene, and a merge helper that keeps both sides' distinct elements.
Running the auth + persistence suite to confirm the conflict and merge paths.

content.text: Done. Summary: /api/auth/login issues an HMAC-signed httpOnly cookie verified by lib/auth/session.ts; /api/canvas/[id] does optimistic autosave keyed on a monotonic version; and the conflict path returns 409 with the full server scene so the client merges (last-writer-wins per element id, server base) instead of overwriting. Storage is behind a saveScene/loadScene adapter so it stays provider-agnostic. Tests cover the signed-cookie, tamper-rejection, stale-409, and merge cases. Handoff: wire the client's reconnect to call mergeScenes on a 409 and re-PUT with the new baseVersion; that re-submit loop isn't built yet.
